advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Distinguish a genuinely-absent HEAD path from an unexpected git error in _blob_shas's per-path fallback rather than mapping both to the 'absent' sentinel.
evidence: completion_verdict_cache.py:109-113: `lines = _rev_parse_lines(...); shas.append(lines[0].strip() if lines else _ABSENT_BLOB_SENTINEL)` — _rev_parse_lines returns None on OSError/SubprocessError/nonzero-returncode alike

docstring at completion_verdict_cache.py:104-105 asserts a per-path failure 'means that ONE path is absent from HEAD (the git-health probe already ran)' — but the health probe only checked HEAD^{tree}, not that each per-path failure is specifically an absence
advisory.finding: _blob_shas's per-path fallback maps ANY failing `git rev-parse HEAD:<path>` to the '_ABSENT_BLOB_SENTINEL' string, conflating a transient/unexpected git failure with a genuinely-absent path — contradicting the docstring claim that 'a failure means that ONE path is absent from HEAD'. A present file transiently unresolvable would be fingerprinted identically to an absent one.
scenarios: A file exists at HEAD but its per-path rev-parse fails transiently (e.g., a race with a concurrent git operation) after the batch already succeeded/failed — its real blob sha is silently replaced by the 'absent' sentinel

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the cross-run PASS cache is only populated via the recovery _finalize path is intended, and that a healthy-primary PASS never needing the cache is acceptable.
evidence: Only call site: `search_files persist_pass_verdicts` → completion_recovery.py:735 inside `_finalize`
completion_recovery.py:718-736 `_finalize` docstring: 'Finalize a FULL-COVERAGE verdict from the bank' — reached on the recovery/finalizer path, not the healthy primary
module docstring completion_verdict_cache.py:3-4 says 'persists each VALIDATED PASS record at finalize' — 'finalize' here is a recovery-path concept, not the primary path
advisory.finding: persist_pass_verdicts is only invoked from the recovery-path _finalize (completion_recovery.py:735); the healthy primary verify path that PASSes without exhaustion never writes to the cross-run cache. If the design intends the cache to seed subsequent runs, a ticket that always PASSes on the primary (never recovers) will never populate the cache, so the cache only ever helps tickets that have exhausted at least once.
scenarios: A ticket verifies PASS on the primary run (no exhaustion); a later re-verify still re-proves everything because nothing was cached

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a persist test: a merged record met=True whose bank entry has met=True AND evidence_sufficient=False is NOT written to the cache.
evidence: completion_verdict_cache.py persist_pass_verdicts: `if entry.get("evidence_sufficient") is False: continue  # PASS-only`
test_completion_verdict_cache.py:220-240 only exercises the met=False/downgrade skip; the docs-updated bank entry there is met=False, not a met=True+insufficient entry

the merged record for the insufficiency case is met=False, so the earlier `record.get('met') is True` filter already excludes it — the evidence_sufficient guard line is never reached by an existing test
advisory.finding: persist_pass_verdicts skips caching a bank entry that is met=True but carries evidence_sufficient=False (the insufficiency guard), but no test isolates this branch — the existing persist test only reaches the skip via a met=False record. A regression dropping the `if entry.get('evidence_sufficient') is False: continue` guard would cache an insufficiency-marked PASS undetected.
scenarios: A criterion the merged verdict scored met=True whose bank entry carries evidence_sufficient=False must not be cached.
advisory.suggested_fix: Construct bank_entries with {criterion_id: {met: True, evidence_sufficient: False}} and a merged verdict record met=True for the same criterion; assert persist_pass_verdicts returns 0 and no .json is written.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the seeded-PASS override of a same-run met=false downgrade cannot mask a regression whose triggering file lies outside the ticket's declared file_impact fingerprint scope.
evidence: completion_verdict_assembly.py:176-188: `if entry is not None and entry.get("seeded") and entry.get("met") is True:` appends a met=True record and `continue`s, bypassing the finalizer's `existing` record entirely (including a met=false downgrade)

completion_verdict_cache.py:123-139 scoped_content_fingerprint hashes only `_normalize_impact(ticket.get("file_impact"))` (or direct-child impacts, or whole-tree only when childless+empty) — a criterion whose correctness depends on a file outside file_impact is not covered
docstring pin at completion_verdict_cache.py:19-20: 'an in-scope edit rotates a blob and invalidates; an unrelated commit does not' — an out-of-scope regression is treated as 'unrelated'
dropped.finding: A seeded (cross-run cached) PASS unconditionally overrides a same-run finalizer met=false downgrade, but the cache-invalidation fingerprint is scoped strictly to the ticket's declared file_impact paths (or child impacts / whole-tree). A regression introduced in a file NOT listed in file_impact does not rotate the fingerprint, so the stale cached PASS is credited verbatim and the current-run downgrade is discarded — masking a genuine regression.
scenarios: A criterion proved PASS in run 1; a later same-scope re-verify legitimately detects the criterion is now broken by an edit to a file the ticket never declared in file_impact — the seeded PASS overrides the downgrade to PASS

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a merge test: one seeded criterion credited over a downgrade AND one genuinely-unmet non-seeded criterion → merged verdict FAIL (any_unmet wins over seeded_override).
evidence: assembly.py:218-223: `if any_unmet: merged["verdict"] = "FAIL"` then `elif seeded_override: ... "PASS"` — precedence branch
test_completion_verdict_cache.py:329-358 `test_finalizer_cannot_downgrade_or_drop_a_seeded_record` asserts all records met and merged verdict PASS; both seeded criteria end met=True
search for `any_unmet` in tests/ returns (no matches) — the FAIL-wins-over-seeded_override branch is unasserted
dropped.finding: No test exercises the merge branch where a seeded PASS is credited over a finalizer downgrade WHILE a different (non-seeded) criterion is genuinely unmet — the any_unmet FAIL must take precedence over the seeded_override PASS. Only the all-records-met path is tested, so a regression flipping this precedence (e.g. making seeded_override force PASS even with an unmet criterion) would go undetected.
scenarios: A run where one criterion is credited from the cross-run cache (seeded) but another criterion the finalizer legitimately marks unmet — the overall verdict must be FAIL, not PASS.
dropped.suggested_fix: Add a test with two criteria: a seeded entry the finalizer downgraded (credited back to met=True) plus a second criterion the finalizer returns met=False with no seeded entry; assert merged['verdict'] == 'FAIL' and the second record stays met=False.
